owner.occupation: River guide running longtail boat tours

world.bio: I run longtail boat tours on the Mekong out of Chiang Khong, in northern Thailand, right where the river bends toward Laos. My family fished the Mekong for three generations. I went to Chiang Mai for university, studied tourism, came back after graduation. I speak Thai, Northern Thai, English, and a bit of Lao. Half proud, half embarrassed of fishing, I do not talk much about it with guests.
skills_assets: A longtail boat for up to eight guests, with a 4-stroke engine, safety certificate and insurance
Local knowledge of the Mekong from Chiang Khong to Sop Ruak, including sandbars, fish habitats, and where the Giant Mekong Catfish used to be caught
Fluent English, good Lao and Chinese at tourist level
A Facebook page about local street food in Chiang Khong, 6,000 followers
A small network of food stalls and homestays along the river
My family's old fishing nets and traps, some of them 40 years old, stored in the garage

projects.name: Sunrise river tour
projects.text: A morning tour that leaves at 5:30, floats down the river to watch the mist and fishermen at work. 800 baht per person, minimum four. I run it three times a week in high season. After the tour guests eat khao soi at a stall my aunt used to run. Bookings are up slightly this year, but the engine is old and I need to save for a replacement, about 45,000 baht.

projects.name: Chiang Khong Food Map
projects.text: I want to map street food stalls around town and publish a small guide for travellers, maybe printed and kept on the boat. It is more a hobby but guests keep asking. I have photos of thirty stalls. The text part is not done. My writing in English is fine but I want it to sound local, not like a brochure.

notes.text: The river is high this week because of rain upstream. Cancelled two tours. A group of Germans were disappointed, but I explained, and they agreed to come the day after. The Mekong is not something you argue with.

Went to Chiang Rai to see my girlfriend. We ate noodles and walked around the night market. She asked me when I would take her on my boat. I said when the engine is fixed. She said that is an excuse. She is right, partly.

A guest asked me today whether my family still fishes. I said 'a little' and changed the subject. Why do I do that? My father fished, my grandfather fished, and I still say 'a little' like it's something small. Maybe I'm afraid people will think we're poor.
Spent the afternoon cleaning the engine with my cousin. He said it needs a new carburetor at least. Quoted 12,000 baht. I have 9,000. I told him to wait until the end of the month.

Posted a photo of tom kha kai from a stall near the bus station on the Facebook page. 400 likes in one hour, a record. People in the comments argued about whether coconut milk should be added at the end or the start. It's the best part of running that page.

Visited my aunt for her birthday. She has a tin box in her house with school exercise books, yellow with age. My father's side of the family wrote the daily fish catches in them since 1987, in pencil. I had not looked at them in ten years. Opened one: '12 June 1993: 4 pla buek, 1 pla nin.' It made me laugh and almost cry.

Made a plan to ask Aunt if I can borrow the exercise books for a few days. I'm not sure why. They are just old notes, but I feel they are something. Maybe I can use them in my tour somehow, but my English guests will not care about the numbers.
Drank too much Leo beer with friends at the riverside bar. One of them asked if I would ever go back to being a fisherman. I said no. Then went home and looked at my father's boat for an hour.

Tourists from Bangkok arrived on the long weekend. Took two boats out, worked 12 hours. Back home my back hurt. My mother put a hot towel on it and said 'you are a fisherman after all.' I said nothing but felt warm.

messages.text:
Nok: When are you coming again?
Me: Next Sunday.
Nok: Bring fish.
Me: I will bring khao soi.

Pong: The engine will die soon.
Me: I know.
Pong: There is a second-hand one in Chiang Saen for 30,000.
Me: Let me check my savings.

Pa Noi: Come eat, I made laab.
Me: I'll come Sunday.
Pa Noi: Bring your cousin too.
Me: Okay.

Klaus: Beautiful tour. Is there any history of fishing in your family?
Me: Yes, but nothing special.
Klaus: I'd love to hear about it next time.
Me: Maybe.

Mum: Did you eat?
Me: Yes, Mae.
Mum: Your father is asking about the exercise books at Pa Noi's. He wants to look at them.
Me: I'll bring them over.

calendar.event: Engine inspection, workshop in Chiang Saen

relations.about: My father's older sister. Keeps the tin box of old fishing notebooks. Runs a small khao soi stall.
Lives in Chiang Rai, works at a dental clinic.

constraints: Tours depend on river level, in rainy season they get cancelled
Boat holds eight, so large groups are not possible
Cannot cross into Laos waters without a permit
Only available mornings and sunset on most days
sensitive: Embarrassed about family's fishing past, although proud privately
Short on money for the engine

disclosure_policy.t0_public: Name, tour business, route, how long family fished the river
disclosure_policy.t1_after_signal: Tour details, sunrise route, old fishing notebooks at my aunt's house
disclosure_policy.t2_after_trust: Feelings about the family past, money for the engine
